headline: Evaluation design, not model novelty, increasingly determines credibility of omics-based clinical prediction
label: Validation Design In Prediction
summary: New studies show metric choice and same-modality validation can inflate performance, while cross-platform and cross-cohort tests expose how fragile it is.
synthesis: The common thread is that reported predictive performance depends heavily on how models are validated. Mammography risk work shows AUC and C-index are insensitive to diagnosis timing, motivating a two-stage whether-versus-when model. The glioblastoma miRNA study finds generative augmentation looks strong under same-modality validation but falls to roughly 0.40-0.47 AUROC across platforms. Other items test generalization more directly: PRTS applies in-context learning across diseases and platforms without per-cohort training, SNOWS transfers to CGGA with C-index 0.691 to 0.712, and anchor-based batch correction avoids covariates. The plasma proteomics framework evaluates compact panels across 23 diseases. What is new is the explicit pairing of cross-platform and timing-aware evaluation with method claims.
